question: How did they pray: set hours, set prayers, facing east?

answers.label: The Lord's Prayer three times a day
At set hours: morning, third, sixth, ninth, evening
Facing east, toward the rising light

overview.text: The Didache, about 100, tells Christians to say the Lord's Prayer three times a day and to fast on Wednesday and Friday.
By about 200, Christians kept the third, sixth and ninth hours, from Acts, plus prayer at dawn and at sunset: the pattern of the later daily office.
They prayed facing east, toward the rising light, which pagans mistook for sun worship.

quotes.author: Didache
quotes.english: Do not let your fasts be with the hypocrites: they fast on the second and fifth day of the week, but you fast on the fourth day and the day of Preparation. Nor pray as the hypocrites, but as the Lord commanded in his Gospel, pray this way: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name ... for yours is the power and the glory for ever. Pray this way three times a day.
quotes.original: Αἱ δὲ νηστεῖαι ὑμῶν μὴ ἔστωσαν μετὰ τῶν ὑποκριτῶν. νηστεύουσι γὰρ δευτέρᾳ σαββάτων καὶ πέμπτῃ: ὑμεῖς δὲ νηστεύσατε τετράδα καὶ παρασκευήν. μηδὲ προσεύχεσθε ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταί, ἀλλ’ ὡς ἐκέλευσεν ὁ κύριος ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ αὐτοῦ, οὕτω προσεύχεσθε: Πάτερ ἡμῶν ὁ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου ... ὅτι σοῦ ἐστιν ἡ δύναμις καὶ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας. τρὶς τῆς ἡμέρας οὕτω προσεύχεσθε.
quotes.context: The Lord's Prayer three times a day, with a closing doxology, and fasting on Wednesday and Friday.

quotes.author: Tertullian
quotes.english: As to time, there will be no idleness in outwardly keeping certain hours, I mean those common ones that mark the divisions of the day, the third, sixth and ninth, which we find more solemn in the Scriptures. The Holy Spirit was first poured on the gathered disciples at the third hour. Peter, on the day he saw the vision of the vessel, had gone up to pray at the sixth hour. He and John went into the temple at the ninth.
quotes.original: De tempore uero non erit otiosa extrinsecus obseruatio etiam horarum quarundam, istarum dico communium quae diei interspatia signant, tertia, sexta, nona; quas sollemniores in scripturis inuenire est. primus spiritus sanctus congregatis discipulis hora tertia infusus est. Petrus, qua die uisionem communitatis omnis in illo uasculo expertus est, sexta hora orandi gratia ascenderat in superiora. idem cum Iohanne ad nonam in templum adibat
quotes.context: Tertullian adds the "lawful" prayers at the beginning of day and night.

quotes.author: Cyprian of Carthage
quotes.english: But for us, dear brothers, besides the hours of prayer kept from of old, both the times and the mysteries of prayer have now increased. For we must pray in the morning, so that the Lord's resurrection may be celebrated by morning prayer ... and again at sunset and the close of day.
quotes.original: Sed nobis, fratres dilectissimi, praeter horas antiquitus obseruatas orandi nunc et spatia et sacramenta creuerunt. nam et mane orandum est, ut resurrectio Domini matutina oratione celebretur. ... recedente item sole ac die cessante necessario
quotes.context: Morning and evening, added to the third, sixth and ninth hours: the outline of the later daily office.

quotes.author: Origen of Alexandria
quotes.english: Now a few words about the direction one should face when praying. There are four directions, north and south, west and east. Who would not at once agree that the east plainly shows that we should turn that way, symbolically, as the soul looks toward the rising of the true light, when we make our prayers?
quotes.original: Ἤδη δὲ xal περὶ τοῦ κλίματος, εἰς ὃ ἀφορῶντα εὖ- χεσϑαι δεῖ, ὀλίγα λεχτέον. τεσσάρων» δὲ ὄντων κλιμάτων, τοῦ τε πρὸς ἄρχτον καὶ μεσημβρίαν καὶ τοῦ πρὸς δύσιν καὶ ἀνατολὴν, τίς οὐκ αν αὐτόϑεν ὁμολογήσαι τὸ πρὸς ἀνατολὴν ἐναργῶς ἐμφαίνειν τὸ δεῖν ἐκεῖ νεύοντας συμβολικῶς, ... τῆς ψυχῆς ἐνορώσης τῇ τοῦ ἀληϑινοῦ φωτὸς ἀνατολῇ, ποιεῖσϑαι τὰς εὐχάς;
quotes.context: Origen says one should face east even if the house's door opens another way.

quotes.author: Tertullian
quotes.english: Hence the suspicion, because it has become known that we pray toward the east.
quotes.original: denique inde suspicio, quod innotuerit nos ad orientis regionem precari.
quotes.context: Pagans took this as sun worship. Tertullian denies it.

quotes.author: Basil of Caesarea
quotes.english: The appointed times of prayer in the brotherhoods must not be passed over, times which we have necessarily chosen... Dawn first, so that the first movements of the soul and of the mind may be offerings to God... At the third hour, to rise for prayer and gather the brotherhood together... reminded of the gift of the Spirit, given to the apostles at the third hour, to worship all with one accord... At the sixth hour we judged prayer to be necessary, in imitation of the saints... The ninth hour has been handed down to us by the apostles themselves in Acts as necessary for prayer... When the day is complete, thanksgiving for what was given us in it... Midnight was handed down to us by Paul and Silas as necessary for prayer... And we must rise for prayer before dawn.
quotes.original: παρορᾶσθαι δεῖ τοὺς διατετυπωμένους καιροὺς τῶν προσευχῶν ἐν ταῖς ἀδελφότησιν, οὓς ἀναγκαίως ἐξελεξάμεθα ... τὸν μὲν ὄρθρον, ὥστε τὰ πρῶτα κινήματα τῆς ψυχῆς καὶ τοῦ νοῦ ἀναθήματα εἶναι Θεοῦ ... κατὰ τὴν τρίτην ὥραν εἰς τὴν προσευχὴν ἀνίστασθαι, καὶ ἐπισυνάγειν τὴν ἀδελφότητα ... τῆς τοῦ Πνεύματος δωρεᾶς, τῆς κατὰ τὴν τρίτην ὥραν τοῖς ἀποστόλοις δεδομένης, προσκυνῆσαι πάντας ὁμοθυμαδόν ... Ἐν δὲ τῇ ἕκτῃ ὥρᾳ κατὰ μίμησιν τῶν ἁγίων ἀναγκαίαν εἶναι τὴν προσευχὴν ἐκρίναμεν ... Ἡ δὲ ἐννάτη παρ’ αὐτῶν ἡμῖν τῶν ἀποστόλων ἐν ταῖς Πράξεσιν ἀναγκαία εἰς προσευχὴν παραδέδοται ... Συμπληρωθείσης δὲ τῆς ἡμέρας, ἡ εὐχαριστία περὶ τῶν ἐν αὐτῇ δεδομένων ἡμῖν ... Τὸ δὲ μεσονύκτιον Παῦλος καὶ Σίλας ἡμῖν ἀναγκαῖον εἰς προσευχὴν παραδεδώκασιν ... χρὴ προφθάσαντας τὸν ὄρθρον εἰς τὴν προσευχὴν διανίστασθαι
quotes.context: Basil's rule for monastic communities (the Asceticon). Question 37 asks about the times of prayer; in the library's locked text the answer begins at the end of the preceding section, so the quote is drawn from sections 36 and 37 together. The day is framed by prayer at dawn, the third, sixth and ninth hours, at the day's end, at midnight and before dawn: the skeleton of the later daily office.

gaps.author: Hippolytus (attributed)
gaps.why: The hours of prayer including midnight.
